fields.meta_title: Post Meeting Survey Questions Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build post meeting survey questions for standups, client calls, all-hands, and recurring meeting reviews, saved to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build Post Meeting Survey Questions That Fix the Next Meeting
fields.hero_description: Build post meeting survey questions that reach attendees as the meeting ends and save every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Post-Meeting Survey
fields.features_subheading: Describe the meeting once, and Emergent builds the survey attendees answer and the table that stores every reply.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your meeting

Name the meeting, such as a team sync or a client kickoff call. Emergent drafts questions to fit it, with one rating scale and one open question, and a prompt rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Sent the minute the meeting ends

Set the end time, and the app posts the survey link in the team's Slack channel or emails each attendee. Anyone who has not answered by the end of the day gets a single reminder.
fields.feature_3:
Names kept off the answers

Turn on anonymous mode, and the survey stores each answer with no name beside it. The app keeps a separate list of who has replied, so reminders go only to people who have not.
fields.feature_4:
Every answer in a database you own

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the meeting and its date. Put four weeks of ratings for one meeting side by side and see whether the change you made helped.
fields.feature_5:
A flag when an answer needs a reply

Set a rule such as any meeting rating of 2 or lower out of 5. The app then emails the meeting owner that same afternoon, with the attendee's comment quoted in the message.
fields.feature_6:
On your domain, in GitHub on paid plans

Run the survey on your own domain, included in Emergent and billed in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep working on it like any app.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your Meeting Survey With Emergent?
fields.why_description: Emergent sets no cap on responses, and you own the data. When the meeting changes, one prompt changes the survey.

fields.tab_content_1:
The Thursday sync loses its status round

At 10:30 on Thursday, the Penrick Analytics sync ends, and the app posts 3 questions in the data team's Slack channel. By 11:00, 8 of the 9 people on the team had answered, and 5 of the 8 said the status round ran too long. The team lead moved status updates to a written thread and kept the sync for decisions.
fields.tab_content_2:
Unclear owners flagged and fixed with an action list

Selkirk Studio emails the client 4 questions after every kickoff call. Any No on whether next steps and owners are clear emails the account lead. After the Hollisford Bakery kickoff, 2 of the 3 bakery staff on the call said No. That afternoon, the account lead sent an action list with an owner beside each task.
fields.tab_content_3:
Next all-hands Q&A runs 20 minutes

Varenne Supply's all-hands survey goes to all 140 staff on the first Friday of each month, with no names stored. Staff answer on their phones, one question per screen. After March, 112 of 140 replied, and 71 of the 112 asked for more time for questions. The April all-hands set aside 20 minutes for Q&A.
fields.tab_content_4:
Calvero retires the Monday meeting its staff rated lowest

For four weeks, Calvero Software's chief of staff asked one question after each recurring meeting: was it a good use of your time? The Monday status meeting got a Yes in 6 of 31 answers, the design review in 22 of 24. She replaced the Monday meeting with a written update posted at 9:00.

faq_plan.q: What are post meeting survey questions?
How do I create post meeting survey questions?

plan.angle: The top 10 for post meeting survey questions are question lists and template pages (ClickUp, Polly, Mentimeter, Slido, SmartSurvey) plus several post-event lists that drift off the meeting intent. None shows a survey going out at the end of a real meeting or what the answers changed. This page shows four post-meeting surveys built from a prompt and run to a decision: a weekly team sync pulse in Slack, a client kickoff check that flags unclear next steps, an anonymous all-hands survey answered on phones, and a four-week review of recurring meetings that cancels one. The how-to gives the writing rules, and the FAQ carries sample questions by meeting type, timing, anonymity and length.
tab_stories: Penrick Analytics posts 3 questions to its 9-person data team's Slack channel when the Thursday sync ends at 10:30, 8 of 9 answer, 5 of 8 say the status round ran long, and the team lead moves status updates to a written thread.

Selkirk Studio asks its client 4 questions after every kickoff call, and when 2 of 3 people at Hollisford Bakery answer No to whether next steps and owners are clear, the account lead gets an email and sends a written action list that afternoon.

Varenne Supply's 140 staff answer an anonymous all-hands survey on their phones, one question per screen, 112 of 140 respond, 71 of 112 ask for more Q&A time, and the next all-hands doubles Q&A to 20 minutes.

Calvero Software's chief of staff asks one question after each of 4 recurring meetings for four weeks, the Monday status meeting is rated a good use of time by 3 of 14 answers, and it is replaced by a written update.
